Basic usage-based billing, built on the Billing Meters API, is a lower-level primitive that remains fully supported for existing integrations.
Meter events represent actions that customers take in your system. You can use meter events to bill a customer based on their usage.
You can use webhook events to monitor and handle transitions between statuses.
A Subscription represents the product details associated with the plan that your customer subscribes to. Allows you to charge the customer on a recurring basis
Stripe Billing supports per-user, per-usage, and per-tier subscription models in an automated recurring billing fashion, covering the 3 standard SaaS pricing approaches.
For multi-currency subscriptions, Stripe PM confirmed you currently need to create a separate plan per currency (e.g. bronze_plan:eur), since Stripe wants merchants to control FX rates intentionally.

User complaint: 'Does this mean I can still create classic subscriptions free of the 0.4% surcharge and process them myself? Edit: The answer is no. This announcement has burnt through a lot of goodwill.'
Billing pricing was clarified: Payments cost 2.9%+$0.30 per charge, while Billing costs 0.4% after the first $1M in recurring subscription charges, on top of payment fees.
Comparison: Recurly charges 1.25% + $0.10 per transaction plus $99-299/month; Stripe Billing's 0.4% fee (free under $1M) was seen by some as a better deal than Recurly's model.
A team said they were 'writing code to move from stripe to recurly/adyen' citing that 'the analytics/easy plan mgmt and email invoicing in recurly is something stripe doesn't have.'
Stripe Billing PM stated all customer emails (like credit card update notices) are off by default, matching behavior of other Stripe emails, so merchants can use their own webhooks instead.
Complaint: 'Managing your subscriptions (recurring charges) via Stripe cost 0.5% - on top of the payment fees' impacting all SaaS using Stripe Billing.

Confusion among users about what Stripe Billing actually includes: 'I thought Stripe Billing referred to the Customer Portal functionality and some advanced Stripe Checkout features... Can anyone clarify?'
Reaction to the new Billing fee: 'If we knew it's gonna cost us an extra .5% of revenue, we would have built our own billing system instead of hacking one around Stripe.'

Stripe email to Starter Plan customers: pricing changes from 0.5% to 0.7% of Billing volume, with the old rate honored for one year until June 30, 2025; a new subscription-based pricing option was also introduced.
User reaction to the fee hike: 'That's a 40% price increase. I've never seen such a drastic increase, not even from Paypal.'
Clarification: Starter plan was 0.5%, Scale plan was 0.8%; both were consolidated into a single 0.7% plan, making it bad news for Starter customers but good news for Scale customers.

Complaint about Billing fee structure: 'There is no reason why this feature is % based... 0.7% just to trigger a charge every month it makes no sense. For international card is 0.7%+3.9%=4.6% fee for payment!'

Long-time user comment: 'as a years-long customer for whom prices keep increasing while product keeps getting worse (fraud detection and dispute handling in particular), I'm really hopeful that a decent competitor shows up soon.'
